title: Geomorphological Configuration and Environmental Connectivity in Two Contrasting Marine-Coastal Geosystems on the Southern Peruvian Coast: La Huata and Carrizales
content: Coastal geosystems emerge from interactions among geomorphology, hydrodynamics, sediment dynamics, geological materials, and groundwater discharge, yet these components are often examined separately. This study compares La Huata and Carrizales, two nearby marine-coastal geosystems on the arid southern Peruvian coast that share a regional climatic, geological, and oceanographic setting but differ markedly in land-sea configuration. Geomatic surveys, field observations, bathymetric and oceanographic measurements, sediment analyses, SEM-EDS characterization, and hydrogeochemical analyses of coastal springs were integrated through a comparative conceptual framework. La Huata forms a partly enclosed, mixed rock-sand embayment, whereas Carrizales combines a predominantly rocky-cliffed shore with an inland aeolian dune system. Conductivity, total dissolved solids, and salinity of marine waters were similar, but oxidation-reduction potential (218.5 versus 175.5 mV) and chlorophyll a (1.67 versus 0.07 µg L⁻¹) were higher at La Huata during the surveys. Coastal springs showed stronger differentiation: La Huata had higher total dissolved solids (4730 versus 850 mg L⁻¹) and nitrate concentrations (140.87 versus 9.17 mg L⁻¹). Beach sands at La Huata were granulometrically heterogeneous, whereas the Carrizales dune transect was consistently dominated by the No. 60 sieve fraction (85.60-95.43%). These converging lines of evidence indicate that local geomorphological configuration acts as a spatial mediator of hydrodynamic, sedimentary, and hydrogeochemical connectivity rather than as a single deterministic control. Although the field campaigns provide temporal snapshots, the integrated approach offers a transferable framework for comparing environmentally contrasting geosystems along arid coasts.
